en.title: Montreal tries to recover from a historic collapse, with Suzuki a question mark
en.deck: Montreal led Winnipeg 4-0 with under three minutes left on Tuesday and lost 5-4 in overtime, ending a five-game win streak. Utah arrives at 10-6-0, scoring and conceding plenty, and captain Nick Suzuki may or may not be back. The model and the market both lean Utah slightly.
news: Coach Martin St-Louis would not commit on Wednesday to Suzuki facing Utah. Suzuki has been out since Oct. 20 and his 546-game ironman streak is over.
Ivan Demidov skated on Tuesday and could resume training with the team next week. Mike Matheson is expected to miss about two weeks, and Kirby Dach missed Tuesday with an illness.
Jacob Fowler made 42 saves on Tuesday, so the goalie is an open question. The site's tracker leans to Jakub Dobes; neither team had named a starter at last check.
Utah beat Toronto 3-2 on Tuesday. John Marino and Maveric Lamoureux are on injured reserve, and Kailer Yamamoto is day-to-day.
records: Winnipeg's four goals came in 2:06, called the latest four-goal comeback in NHL history. Caufield said there was no excuse for it.
Cole Caufield scored twice on Tuesday, has 10 goals and has now scored against every NHL team.
Clayton Keller leads Utah with 21 points (17 assists) but has gone six games without a goal. Logan Cooley has five goals in his last five.
Twelve of Utah's 16 games have gone over 5.5 goals, and the last six meetings averaged 6.5.

news: Coach Jeff Blashill said some players played at the end of their stick and that the team needs all 20 going. He praised Connor Bedard's effort and is under growing scrutiny, with The Hockey News naming him and GM Kyle Davidson on its hot-seat list.

Yanni Gourde (hip) misses this one but could return on the coming road trip. Nikita Kucherov has asked for a trade, AP reported last week.

records: Kochetkov became the third goalie in NHL history to win his first 10 starts of a season.

en.title: Model and market split on a Dallas team likely without Heiskanen
en.deck: Jason Robertson scored a natural hat trick and Mikko Rantanen reached 800 points in Tuesday's 6-5 win in Washington, but Miro Heiskanen was hurt on a hit. Columbus just beat Colorado 7-2. This is the only game tonight where the model and the market pick different favourites.
news: Heiskanen is day-to-day and will likely miss Thursday; Thomas Harley would be the obvious power-play replacement. He has 11 points in 15 games.
Matt Duchene is out about three months after core surgery. Radek Faksa is back from a lower-body injury.
Charlie Coyle had four points against Colorado, and Valeri Nichushkin scored against his former team.
Cam Talbot made 27 saves on Tuesday; the site's tracker leans to Jet Greaves tonight and Jake Oettinger for Dallas. Neither is confirmed. Isac Lundestrom is out for Columbus.
records: Rantanen is the fourth Finn with 800 NHL points. Robertson's three goals in 5:20 were the third-fastest hat trick in Stars history.
Dallas has points in five straight road games (4-0-1) and won the Oct. 31 meeting 3-1.
Zach Werenski has no goal in 17 games but six assists in a four-game point streak; the model flags him as due. Conor Garland has no goal in 27.
Only 4 of Dallas' 15 games have gone over 5.5 goals. Coach Rick Bowness's team is 4-3-0 at home.
betting: Market: Stars 1.79, Blue Jackets 2.07, about 54–46 without the margin. The model has Columbus 51–49, the only game tonight with different favourites.

en.title: Fresh from a record comeback, Winnipeg hosts 3-13-1 Vancouver
en.deck: Winnipeg ended a nine-game losing streak on Tuesday by scoring four goals in 2:06 and winning in overtime in Montreal. Vancouver arrives at 3-13-1, allowing 4.53 goals a game, with three straight losses. The market likes the Jets far more than the model does.
news: Josh Morrissey (wrist) is out again but has not been ruled out for Sunday. Nick Bjugstad and Vladislav Namestnikov are also out.
Coach Scott Arniel said Tuesday's win felt like a playoff win. The Hockey News put him on its hot-seat list on Saturday.
Filip Chytil did not travel, and Tom Willander is day-to-day. Thatcher Demko is hoped back before Christmas.
Stuart Skinner and Leevi Meriläinen are the site's likely starters. It is the teams' first meeting of the season.
records: The comeback was the latest four-goal rally in NHL history and the fastest four goals in Jets history. Kyle Connor scored twice with the goalie pulled, and Dylan Samberg won it.
The Canucks allow 4.53 goals a game. Winnipeg is only 2-4-1 at home, and it lost 7-0 in Carolina two days before the comeback.
Mark Scheifele has 12 assists but 2 goals, none in eight games. The model flags him and Gabriel Vilardi as due.
Jonathan Lekkerimäki has 6 goals and 7 assists in his last ten, and Jake DeBrusk scored twice against Anaheim.

en.title: McDavid's historic start meets a Ducks team that can't stop scoring or conceding
en.deck: Connor McDavid has a point in all 16 games and 40 points overall, a pace only Lemieux, Gretzky and Joe Malone have matched. Anaheim comes in after Cutter Gauthier's hat trick in a 5-4 win in Vancouver. The market expects a shootout, more so than the model.
news: Edmonton's goalie is unconfirmed. Tristan Jarry has allowed three goals on his last 76 shots; the site's tracker leans to Matt Tomkins, and Devon Levi could be close.

Anaheim is without Troy Terry, Ryan Poehling, A.J. Greer and Ian Moore. Lukas Dostal is the likely starter.
Edmonton won the Oct. 7 meeting 5-2 with two goals from Evan Bouchard.
records: McDavid leads the NHL with 31 assists and has an assist in every game this season. Leon Draisaitl has 13 goals.
Ryan Nugent-Hopkins became Edmonton's all-time leader in games played on Tuesday, at 1,038.
Anaheim has gone 3-6-1 in its last ten and allows 4.2 goals a game in that span. Twelve of its 15 games have gone over 5.5.
Bouchard has an eight-game road point streak, and the last 12 meetings averaged 7.9 goals.

en.title: Bednar wants a change after 7-2, and red-hot Forsberg is coming to town
en.deck: Colorado lost 7-2 in Columbus on Tuesday, and coach Jared Bednar called the team's inconsistency a Jekyll-and-Hyde pattern that has to end. Nashville has points in five of six and Filip Forsberg is on a record-tying multipoint run. Model and market both favour the Avalanche, the market more strongly.
news: Bednar said he can't stay patient on the bench when players aren't engaged. Cale Makar said it feels like everything goes wrong once one thing does.
Scott Wedgewood was pulled after allowing four goals on nine shots. Mackenzie Blackwood made 12 saves in relief and is the site's very likely starter.
Josh Manson (ankle) is out for about eight weeks. Jonathan Marchessault missed Tuesday and is day-to-day for Nashville.
Juuse Saros made 29 saves to hand Pyotr Kochetkov his first loss. Shane Wright debuted for Nashville after his trade from Seattle.
records: Forsberg's five straight multipoint games tie Roman Josi's franchise record. He has 11 points in that run.
Nathan MacKinnon has a six-game point streak (3 goals, 8 assists) and 27 points. Artturi Lehkonen has 12 goals, and the model flags his finishing as running hot.
Nashville beat Colorado 6-2 on Oct. 25. Josi tied Scott Niedermayer with 39 game-winning goals, eighth among defensemen.
Twelve of Colorado's 16 games have gone over 5.5, and the last 12 meetings averaged 6.7 goals.
